en: The application is for the purpose of propitiating Mars.
Aṅgāraka (Mars) is the wielder of the spear, red-limbed, and the son of the Earth.
The prince Maṅgala, Bhauma, Mahākāya, and Dhanaprada. || 1 ||
Mars is the remover of debt, the creator of vision, the causer of disease and the destroyer of disease;
he has the luster of lightning, causes wounds, grants desires, and takes away wealth. || 2 ||
He is fond of group singing, wears red garments, and has long reddish eyes;
he is red, of crimson hue, and the awakener of all ritual actions. || 3 ||
Wearing red garlands, adorned with golden earrings, the leader of the planets—any man who constantly recites these names of Bhauma [will attain his favor]. || 4 ||
His debt, misfortune, and poverty are destroyed;
he obtains abundant wealth as well as a charming wife. (5)
He who worships Maṅgala on the day of Mars with many flowers shall obtain a son who illuminates his lineage; of this there is no doubt.
And all suffering caused by the seizing spirits (grahas) will certainly perish for him. || 7 ||
Thus ends the Aṅgāraka-stotra in the glorious Skanda Purāṇa.
